name: Evenki

ancestors.notes: Descent per Glottolog classification of Evenki (even1259).

notes: Research. Evenki is a Northern Tungusic language written in a Cyrillic alphabet (Nedjalkov 1997) that extends Russian with a single extra letter, Ӈ (velar nasal). The base Cyrillic letters are mapped with their usual values (в rendered as the approximant w, as in Evenki); ⟨э⟩ is central [ə] (not close-mid [e]) — the pre-upgrade mapping's largest single error source. Vowel length, phonemic in Evenki, is written with a combining macron over а/э/о (а̄ э̄ о̄) or with the dedicated precomposed letters Ӣ/Ӯ for и/у; all are modelled as long vowels here (Nedjalkov 1997). Word stress is non-contrastive, typically penultimate in the disyllabic-dominant sampled forms; marked here as penultimate by default. A productive native pattern in which н/д/л palatalize (to ɲ/dʒ/lʲ) and drop the following iotated vowel's glide before е/ё/ю/я is attested in the gold (⟨дюганӣ⟩ [dʒuɣaɲiː], ⟨няӈня⟩ [ɲaŋɲa]) but is NOT applied to Russian loanwords, which keep the Russian glide+vowel reading (⟨октябрь⟩ [oktjabrʲ], a borrowed month name) — because the same т/с/к graphemes keep the glide in loans but the pattern cannot be told apart from spelling alone without a loanword/native distinction the engine has no signal for, this palatalization is left unencoded as a known engine-limit gap rather than risk corrupting loanword output. Pervasive vowel harmony is conditioned rather than spelled and is left unencoded.
